key_insight: Training PV forecasting models to predict multiple future time steps at once improves accuracy by helping them learn longer-range temporal dependencies.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more robust, low-overhead forecasting strategy for solar grid operations, improving resilience to intermittent PV power swings.
method: Combine ground-based sky images with historical PV generation data.
Replace single-horizon point prediction with multi-horizon forecasting across discrete future steps.
Compare the approach across multiple deep learning architectures to test architecture-independent gains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative validation across diverse deep learning models, with multi-horizon forecasting improving accuracy and robustness over the full forecast horizon while adding negligible computational overhead.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and alignment of sky imagery and PV time-series inputs, so deployment needs careful data synchronization and missing-data handling.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
